title: Ordinary quotient extension of a literal finite free model complex
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its integral scalar ring $A$, the positive quotient $R_n=A/(\varpi_E^{n+1})$, a scheme $T$, and a normalized encoding $e$ as in [def-sfb-finite-model-quotient-coordinates]. For finite ranks $a,b$ and an arbitrary matrix $v:A^a\to A^b$, form the literal double complex $K=[\operatorname{model}_{A,T}(A^a)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{model}(v)}\operatorname{model}_{A,T}(A^b)]$ in degrees $-1,0$, using the recorded lifted scalar coordinates. Apply ordinary internal-module extension along the actual quotient map, then the ordinary fixed-coordinate encoding $(e.\mathrm{ordinary}\circ e.\mathrm{fixed})$. The resulting cochain complex is isomorphic to the termwise constant realization of the literal scalar complex $[R_n^a\xrightarrow{\bar v}R_n^b]$, with $\bar v$ the entrywise actual quotient. No injectivity or exactness assumption on $v$ is imposed, and zero ranks are included.

proof.text: Construct a scalar-compatible rank-one comparison under the actual quotient and normalized encoding, using the regular-module comparisons.

The integral model, quotient extension and encoding are additive. Compare their finite biproducts with those of the constant-sheaf functor. In the standard Pi coordinates, integralDifferential and differential are biproduct.matrix with entries multiplication by v i j and its actual residue. The rank-one square proves the full differential square by biproduct hom extensionality.

Construct the cochain isomorphism of the mapped double complexes from the two term isomorphisms and their differential square. Outside degrees -1 and 0 both objects are zero. This covers either rank zero using the empty biproduct.

theorem ordinary_free_complex (T : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ) (e : Encoding l E n T)
    (a b : ℕ) (v : Matrix (Fin b) (Fin a) (A l E)) :
    letI := (Padic.coefficientExtensionAbsoluteValue l E).toNormedField
    Nonempty
      ((((e.ordinary.trans e.fixed).functor.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((Mod.extendScalars (AdicCompletion.quotient l E T n)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ)).obj
          (HomologicalComplex.double
            ((FiniteConstantModel.modelFunctor (A l E) T).map
              (integralDifferential l E a b v))
            (c := ComplexShape.up ℤ) (i₀ := -1) (i₁ := 0) (by decide)))) ≅
        (((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (R l E n)))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ)).obj (scalarComplex l E n a b v)))
